newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish governor wants Islamist dress reported.
newsitem.headline: Turkish governor wants Islamist dress reported.

text.p: A Turkish provincial governor said on Thursday Ankara residents should report people seen wearing Islamic-style dress in a move by the secular establishment against religious activism, Anatolian news agency said.

"Inform the governor's office if you see anyone who does not comply with the dress law by wearing robes and turbans on Ankara streets," Ankara Governor Erdogan Sahinoglu was quoted as telling the agency.

The military-dominated National Security Council ordered the government in February to crack down on what it saw as a rise in religious activism since Islamist Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan came to power last June.

The row between Islamists and the powerful secularists was intensified on Wednesday by a top prosecutor's announcement that he was seeking the closure of Erbakan's Welfare Party on the grounds that it endangered the state's secularist principles.
Among the council's demands were tighter implementation of dress restrictions, moves to close unofficial Koran courses and efforts to limit the role of religious schools.
Anatolian quoted the Ankara governor as saying 72 illegal Koran courses had been closed down and 20 newly proposed courses forbidden from opening in Ankara in response to the demands.

The largely Moslem population of Turkey dresses in Western-style clothes. Turkey's dress laws, banning religious style dress, were established by the secularist founder of modern Turkey, Mustafa Kemal Ataturk.
